I'll think through this season as the farmer would.

---

My land is 4.5 mu, split the same every year — wheat in winter, maize in summer, back to back. Forty years of this rotation. I've read enough and talked to enough extension people to know I should think about nutrient balance, but I also know what my soil does and what my yields have been.

**Wheat first.** I planted last October already — Jimai 22, an improved variety my neighbors and I have used for years. It yields me around 480-500 kg/mu in a normal year. Soil here is calcareous loam, decent but needs fertilizer every year.

At sowing I put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15), about 40 kg/mu — that gave me 6 kg N, 6 kg P2O5, 6 kg K2O as base. Now at jointing (春季返青拔节) I'll topdress urea, 20 kg/mu, which gives another ~9 kg N. Total around 15 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. I used to apply more N, but I saw lodging two years ago when I pushed to 18, and the extension station told me split application and moderate N is better. I trust that now.

Irrigation: I have well access, so I'll irrigate at jointing and at grain filling — two times. Winter was dry this year so I may have already done a winter watering, call it three total but the two spring ones are what matter. I'll say 3.

Pesticide: one spray at heading for aphids and powdery mildew, combined with foliar fertilizer. One application is enough most years; I only double up if I see trouble.

Tillage for wheat was rotary after the maize stalks were chopped and returned — standard now, saves labor since it's just the two of us and my wife can't do heavy work anymore.

Expected: 500 kg/mu.

**Maize after wheat.** I'll plant Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid right after wheat harvest in mid-June — no-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble, that's what I've done for six, seven years now. Saves the tractor cost and moisture.

Base fertilizer at sowing: 30 kg/mu of compound 18-18-8 or so, gives about 5-6 kg N base. Topdress urea at big trumpet stage (大喇叭口期), 25 kg/mu, another ~11 kg N. Total ~17 kg N, 5 kg P, 3 kg K per mu. Maize is a heavier N feeder than wheat, and I'd rather put a little extra than see yellow leaves — losing 50 kg/mu of maize costs me far more than an extra bag of urea.

Irrigation: summer rains usually cover most of it, but I'll irrigate once at tasseling if dry, and maybe once at planting. Two times to be safe.

Pesticide: one spray for corn borer around tasseling. Sometimes a second if armyworm shows up, but typically one.

Expected: 600 kg/mu — that's what I've been getting with this hybrid and these rates.

Budget-wise, total fertilizer cost is maybe 600-700 yuan across the 4.5 mu for each crop. It's real money but I'm not cutting corners — both crops pay back when yields hold.
